narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Lexicographer's Page"**

The window is one well-set page of a dictionary. Every Dictionary in the Current Group answers on a single ruled page, each Entry in the typographic voice its own authors gave it, and a thumb index cut into the fore-edge is how the reader moves between them. The interface supplies only what a printed dictionary supplies: a cover, rules, guide words, an index column and a thumb index. Everything else is the Entries.

Density is a feature. A reader comparing four dictionaries wants to see four dictionaries, so the headword column runs full, the page rules run to the fore-edge, and empty space only appears where there is genuinely nothing to show. Colour is almost absent: paper, ink, and one vermilion that only ever means "you are here".

The system was built and reviewed as a clickable prototype in `design/prototype/`. The rules below describe that build. Where the shipped app differs, the build in the app wins and this file is updated.
keyCharacteristics: Ink-black cover band as the title bar; India-paper page beneath it.
Bold serif headwords inside 【 】; system sans for every control.
Structure drawn with rules (a double rule, single hairlines), never with boxed cards.
A half-round thumb index at the right edge, one notch per answering Dictionary.
One vermilion, reserved for the current position.
Keyboard first: every action reachable from the command palette.

rules.name: The You-Are-Here Rule
rules.body: Vermilion marks the reader's current position and nothing else. If an element is not "where you are now", it is not vermilion: not focus rings, not primary buttons, not links, not warnings.

rules.name: The Closed Book Rule
rules.body: The dark theme is designed, not inverted: a navy bookcloth ground, cloth-toned notches and paper-coloured type. The brightest solid in the dark window is the current notch, never the chrome.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif is for words from the dictionary and words the reader typed; sans is for everything the application says. A control label in serif, or a headword in sans, breaks the rule.

rules.name: The Hands-Off Entry Rule
rules.body: OpenDict never sets the type of an Entry. Each Dictionary's HTML and CSS render in their own isolated root, and the app's styling stops at the Dictionary header.

rules.name: The Ruled Page Rule
rules.body: Separate with rules, never with boxes. A double rule closes the page head; a single rule separates Dictionaries; hairlines divide rows. No cards, no nested containers, no shadows on anything inside the page.

dos: **Do** keep vermilion to the current position: selected row, current notch, caret, active-setting checks.
**Do** run the page's double rule and section rules the full width of the page to the thumb index.
**Do** set headwords and typed queries in the serif, and every control label in the system sans.
**Do** show every answering Dictionary on one page, in the Current Group's order, each Entry exactly as its Dictionary styles it.
**Do** give empty and no-match states somewhere to go: the headword index, recent lookups, another Group, a wildcard pattern.
**Do** design the dark theme from bookcloth navy and cloth notches, and keep the current notch the brightest solid.
donts: **Don't** put Entries, settings or lists in cards, boxes or shadowed containers inside the page.
**Don't** use vermilion for focus rings, primary buttons, links or emphasis.
**Don't** restyle, re-font or re-colour an Entry beyond the dark-theme treatment the reader can switch off per Dictionary.
**Don't** leave the headword column or the page mostly empty when there are headwords to show.
**Don't** use gradients, glass effects or glowing borders; the reader asked for none of them.
**Don't** round controls beyond 2px; only the Mini Window, as a real window, takes 8px.
